rows.grounds: points to the words in question
compound: gīr+patīnāṃ (speech-lords), possessors of the words

items.question: By what inherent power are the expansive words of the lords of speech restrained?
premises: The speaker claims to bring restraint.
The restrained objects are the spread-out words.
Those words belong to the lords of speech.
items.inference: The speaker inherently subdues the expansive speech of authoritative teachers.
uncertainties: The identity of the lords of speech is not specified.
items.plain_english: By nature I bring under restraint those spread-out words of the lords of speech.

rows.grounds: first member of repeated compound element
locates the judgment in this context
object attained, here notoriety as laughable

items.question: What status do the enumerations of various doctrines and teachings attain in this context?
premises: There are various enumerations of doctrines and teachings.
These enumerations are considered here.
They attain the fame of laughter.
items.inference: Mere cataloging of diverse doctrinal systems becomes an object of ridicule.
items.plain_english: Here the various enumerations of doctrines, teachings, and so forth become objects of laughter.

items.question: Why do disputants fail to reach a final determination despite offering many arguments?
premises: They have already spoken many arguments.
They seek to determine the matter.
They fall back again as fallen.
items.inference: Repeated argumentation without resolution leaves disputants in a fallen, inconclusive state.
items.plain_english: Even after having spoken many arguments, the fallen ones fall back again, trying to determine the truth.

rows.grounds: points to the defect or duality
one who knows the oneness of reality

items.question: How does passing through doubleness lead to knowledge of the oneness of reality?
premises: A state of doubleness is attained.
She ripens through infinity.
She becomes a knower of the oneness of reality.
items.inference: Maturation through and beyond duality culminates in knowing reality's oneness.
uncertainties: The referent of sā is implicit.
items.plain_english: Having attained that doubleness, she ripens through infinity and becomes a knower of the oneness of reality.

rows.grounds: state not attained by mere multitude

items.question: Why does the merging of light into light differ from a mere multitude of meters attaining self-will?
premises: Light goes into light.
A multitude of meters is contrasted.
That multitude does not attain self-will.
items.inference: True nondual merging is not equivalent to an aggregate plurality gaining autonomy.
uncertainties: The metaphorical link between meters and freedom is compressed.
items.plain_english: Light goes into light; nor does a mere multitude of meters attain self-will.

rows.grounds: relative referring to the praised reality
first member of compound, linguistic manifestation

items.question: What kind of manifest excellence do poets seek in the object whose nature is sphoṭa?
premises: Poets seek excellence.
The sought object is manifest.
Its nature is characterized as sphoṭa and knowable.
items.inference: Poetic excellence is sought in a manifest reality grounded in sphoṭa.
uncertainties: sphoṭa is a technical term retained as transliterated concept.
items.plain_english: Even poets seek that excellence which is manifest as the knowable object whose nature is sphoṭa.

rows.grounds: means by which fulfillment is reached
compound: kṛta+arthatāṃ, state of having achieved the aim
refers to the liberated or fulfilled state

items.question: How does manifestation bring about fulfilled purpose together with accomplished liberation?
premises: Fulfilled purpose is attained through manifestation.
Liberation is accomplished.
That accomplishment is completed.
items.inference: Manifestation culminates in both fulfilled purpose and realized liberation.
uncertainties: The referent of tam is contextually implied.
items.plain_english: Through manifestation it attained fulfilled purpose, having accomplished that liberation.

rows.grounds: first member referring to destructive disputation
reasonings not fallen into such modes

items.question: What distinguishes reasonings that shine clearly from those reduced to mere destructive disputation?
premises: The reasonings belong to someone.
They have not gone to vaitaṇḍika and similar modes.
They are unfolded and shine clearly.
items.inference: Reasonings shine when they are unfolded without collapsing into mere eristic dispute.
items.plain_english: Whose unfolded reasonings, not gone into vaitaṇḍika and the like, shine forth clearly.

rows.grounds: another group affected by the speech

items.question: How does a single authoritative speech direct diverse ascetic groups onto its course?
premises: Multitudes of triple-staff ascetics are affected.
Śāmbaras are likewise affected.
Both become so for the course by that speech.
items.inference: The power of this speech draws different ascetic communities into its path.
uncertainties: The exact identity of śāmbaras is tradition-specific.
items.plain_english: By whose speech multitudes of triple-staff ascetics, and likewise the śāmbaras, were set upon that course.

items.question: What determines whether seekers become absorbed in the pure supreme meaning of this speech or remain impure?
premises: The supreme pure meaning of the speech can be sought.
Some become absorbed to obtain it.
Others are not absorbed or remain impure.
items.inference: Attunement to this speech yields absorption in its pure meaning, while lack of it leaves impurity.
uncertainties: The syntax allows alternative readings of the negations.
items.plain_english: By whose speech some, to obtain its pure supreme meaning, became absorbed, while others did not, or remained impure.

items.question: Why does this composition of meaning not serve a merely personal purpose despite arising from the seed of the Veda and its lord?
premises: The composition does not go for its own purpose.
It is a composition of meaning.
It is linked to the seed of the Veda and so forth of the lord.
items.inference: The speech's meaning-structure is not self-serving but rooted in a transcendent scriptural source.
uncertainties: The exact relation between īśituḥ and bīja is compactly expressed.
items.plain_english: Whose composition of meaning does not go for its own sake, being of the lord who is the seed of the Veda and so forth.

items.question: By what kind of limiting part does this power bind without concealing reality through the inner principle?
premises: Reality is not directly concealed.
Binding occurs by a prior part.
Binding does not occur by the inner-standing part.
items.inference: Limitation operates through an outer prior phase rather than through the innermost reality.
uncertainties: The subject of badhnāti is implicit.
items.plain_english: It does not directly conceal reality; it binds by a prior part, not by the inner one.

rows.grounds: compound: abhisauhitya+vat, compared to wholesome nourishment

items.question: Why does literariness fail to shine when it is reduced merely to qualities like good nourishment?
premises: Literariness is being evaluated.
It does not shine when gone merely to qualities.
It is compared to good nourishment.
items.inference: True literariness exceeds a mere accumulation of pleasing qualities.
uncertainties: The force of abhisauhitya+vat as a simile is interpretive.
items.plain_english: Indeed, literariness does not shine when it is reduced merely to qualities, as if it were just good nourishment.

rows.grounds: compound: accha+dvayena, by the two lips

items.question: How can what is covered by compassionate lips still shine forth?
premises: The mind is agitated with compassion.
The pair of lips covers something.
That covered thing still shines.
items.inference: Compassionate concealment does not extinguish but paradoxically reveals radiance.
uncertainties: The covered referent is not explicitly named.
items.plain_english: How do they shine, covered by the pair of lips of a mind agitated with compassion?

items.question: What makes the five-marked face shine from the very beginning with true power?
premises: The face is five-marked.
It shines from the beginning.
Its radiance is by true power.
items.inference: The five-marked face's splendor is grounded in an inherent true power.
uncertainties: The specific five marks are not enumerated here.
items.plain_english: The five-marked face shines from the very beginning with a radiance of true power.

rows.grounds: those who have cast off egoisms

items.question: How does abandoning the five egoisms relate to the fear arising from fivefold coming and going?
premises: There is a fivefold nature.
There is fear of coming and going.
The five egoisms are abandoned.
items.inference: Freedom from the five egoisms overcomes the fear rooted in fivefold transmigratory existence.
uncertainties: The exact mapping of the five egoisms is not specified.
items.plain_english: Those who have abandoned the five egoisms are beyond the fear of coming and going inherent in fivefold nature.

items.question: What significance lies in the unified garment below the throat shining with majesty?
premises: The garment has become one.
It is below the throat.
It is radiant with majesty.
items.inference: A unified lower adornment becomes a sign of radiant majesty.
uncertainties: Symbolic meaning of the garment is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: That garment below the throat, having become one, shines radiant with majesty.

rows.grounds: first member of compound, river name

items.question: Why is the upward movement in the primeval place compared to Yamunā longing for union with Gaṅgā?
premises: Yamunā desires union with Gaṅgā.
There is upward movement in the primeval place.
The movement is likened to that desire.
items.inference: The ascent is portrayed as a longing-driven movement toward sacred union.
uncertainties: The subject of yānti may be metaphorical.
items.plain_english: Like the Yamunā desiring union with the Gaṅgā, going upward in the primeval place.

rows.grounds: compound: śaila+jā, born of the mountain

items.question: What fulfillment comes to those eager for the touch of the mountain-born forest creeper?
premises: Some are eager for the touch of the mountain-born forest creeper.
Their eagerness is directed toward that contact.
They become fulfilled.
items.inference: Longing for contact with the sacred mountain-born presence results in fulfillment.
uncertainties: The creeper may be symbolic of a divine power.
items.plain_english: Some, eager for the touch of the mountain-born forest creeper, become fulfilled.

items.question: How does the pure ocean of compassion function as manifest guidance for protection?
premises: There is an ocean of compassion.
It is pure and manifest in guidance.
It exists for protection.
items.inference: Compassion manifests as pure guidance that serves to protect.
items.plain_english: For protection, the pure ocean of compassion is a manifest guidance.

items.question: How can true tenderness simultaneously obtain and defeat through its splendor?
premises: Things are obtained and defeated.
This happens always.
It occurs by the splendor of true tenderness.
items.inference: The splendor of true tenderness has the paradoxical power both to win and to overcome.
uncertainties: The objects obtained and defeated are unspecified.
items.plain_english: Indeed, by the splendor of true tenderness, things are always both obtained and defeated.

items.question: Why does the moon's setting yield to the blameless radiance-shadow of the nail lights?
premises: The moon goes to setting.
A blameless state is always present.
The shadow or radiance of nail lights is invoked.
items.inference: Even the moon's brilliance is surpassed by the blameless radiance associated with the nail lights.
uncertainties: The image of nail-light shadow is poetically compressed.
items.plain_english: The moon always sets before the blameless state, the shadow of the light of the nails.

rows.grounds: compound: hata+gatiḥ, whose movement is arrested

items.question: What causes motion to be arrested in approaching the state of the Kailāsa mountain?
premises: A state is to be attained.
Approach has been made.
Motion is stopped in relation to the Kailāsa mountain.
items.inference: Approaching the exalted state of Kailāsa brings ordinary movement to a halt.
uncertainties: The subject whose motion is stopped is implied.
items.plain_english: Approaching to attain that state, with motion stopped, before the mountain of Kailāsa.

rows.grounds: compound: sva+abhyāsam, one's own repeated practice
compound: tri+pathagā, flowing in three paths
negates being merely the heavenly river
compound: āka+āpagā, river of the sky

items.question: How does the three-pathed stream embody beneficial self-practice rather than remaining only a heavenly river?
premises: It bears its own practice.
It bears what is beneficial.
It is three-pathed, like earth, not merely the heavenly river.
items.inference: The three-pathed stream is valued for embodied beneficial practice, not just celestial origin.
uncertainties: The metaphorical identification with earth is suggestive.
items.plain_english: Bearing her own practice and what is beneficial, the three-pathed one is like the earth, not merely the heavenly river.
